Subject: Acme — incoming redlines (MSA + Order Form) / need coordination

Team — forwarding Acme's initial redlines on the MSA + order form (attached). High level asks from Acme: reduce availability to 99.95% for non-production, expand permitted maintenance blackout windows, and a more aggressive credit matrix (they want a 25% credit at 99.5% uptime). Procurement is pushing for these to close this week.

Action items:
- Lauren: legal to review the MSA redline doc and flag any non-starters (esp. SLA metric change and mandatory audit clauses).
- Monica: ops/CS — confirm whether 99.95% / requested maintenance windows are operationally feasible without dedicated capacity changes. Also call out our current on-call/responder SLAs for Severity 1/2.
- Karthik: commercial — how flexible are we on credits vs. contract value? Any precedent?

I put a soft deadline of EOD Wed (6/13) to have proposed internal positions so we can get a counter out before Acme's legal reviews next week. I will loop in John's thread once we have a consolidated position.

Attachments: acme_msa_redlines_v3.docx (docx), orderform_sla_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — Priyom

Thanks, Priyom. Quick review notes (high level) after a skim of acme_msa_redlines_v3.docx:
- The uptime change from 99.9% to 99.95% is a risky change only if they also increase credit depth — they are asking for both (lower SLO + higher credits). We should not accept a materially lower SLO without either a commensurate cue on price or a carve-out for scheduled maintenance agreed up front.
- Their mandatory audit language wants expanded access to logs beyond our typical SOC2 scope. We can offer scoped evidence (SLA reports + trace audit exports) rather than unlimited access.
- Maintenance blackout windows: they want shorter notice periods and multiple blackout windows per quarter. Suggest we propose a single quarterly blackout block with 72 hours notice and an agreed calendar — easier to operationalize.

I will prepare annotated redlines and mark any legal non-starters (including suggested alternative language).

— Lauren

Subject: Acme redlines (MSA v3 & Order Form SLA matrix)

Priyom — appreciate the quick turnaround earlier. Attaching our redlines (sent as docx) and a short comment file. TL;DR from Acme:
- For our critical business processes we need a contractual uptime guarantee of 99.95% (we measured you at 99.97% in our perf tests but we want comfort for non-prod/production parity).
- Requested credits: scale of 10% @ <99.9, 25% @ <99.6, 50% @ <99.0.
- Maintenance: want limited planned maintenance (maximum of 6 windows per year, each no longer than 6 hours) and want at least 48 hours notice — we reduced our previous ask after talking to procurement.
- Response times: want 1 hour initial response for Sev1 and 4 hours for Sev2.

Can Redwood accept 99.95% for production only and keep 99.9% for non-production? If not, can we meet them halfway: 99.9% baseline with a carve for critical accounts to 99.95% if they purchase Dedicated capacity?

We are aiming to finish contracting this month — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Thanks,
John Evans
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Cloud
jevans@acmecloud.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme redlines (MSA v3 & Order Form SLA matrix)

Looping in operational context:
- Our production fleet average availability over last 90 days across hosted regions is 99.97%. 99.95% for production is operationally trivial. Non-production (sandbox) sometimes sees lower availability during heavy CI test loads — keeping non-prod at 99.9% is reasonable.
- Maintenance windows: limiting to 6/year x 6 hours each is workable but impacts our ability to schedule critical kernel/driver updates. If they limit windows, we should require a 5 business-day maintenance calendar lock or allow an additional emergency maintenance clause for critical patches with notice.
- Response SLOs: 1 hour initial for Sev1 is standard; 4 hours for Sev2 is tighter than our current published 8 hours. We can offer 4 hours for customers on Dedicated or on an upgraded support plan (we have precedent with Enterprise Support Add-on).

Suggested internal position to present to Acme:
1) Production uptime: 99.95% (for production workloads) if they sign for Dedicated or commit to a 12-month annual commit on hosted. Otherwise maintain 99.9% for standard hosted.
2) Credits: propose a capped credit pool (max 50% annual credit cap) and move the 25% step to <99.6 only for accounts on Dedicated.
3) Maintenance: allow 6 windows/year (<=6 hours) with a requirement that Acme approves a planned maintenance calendar 5 business days in advance; allow emergency patching with 24-hour notice for security-critical fixes.
4) Response times: 1 hour Sev1; 4 hour Sev2 only for Enterprise Support / Dedicated customers; default 8 hour Sev2 for standard.

If legal is comfortable with the suggested carve-outs (Lauren), I recommend we propose the above as our counter to Acme.

— Monica
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Acme redlines (MSA v3 & Order Form SLA matrix) — Redwood counterproposal

John / Acme team — thanks for the detailed notes and the docx. We've reviewed internally (legal + ops + commercial) and propose the following compromise to help move contracting along quickly:

1) Availability: Redwood will commit to a production SLA of 99.95% for Acme if Acme either (a) purchases Dedicated capacity for the contracted environments, or (b) signs a 12-month committed hosted spend (minimum $150k ARR). For standard hosted without a commit, Redwood's baseline SLA remains 99.9%.

2) Credits: We will accept a tiered credit schedule but must cap annual credits at 50% of one month’s fees (to avoid runaway refunds). Proposed steps: 10% credit for monthly uptime <99.9, 25% credit for monthly uptime <99.6 for Dedicated/Committed accounts, and 50% credit for monthly uptime <99.0.

3) Maintenance: We can lock to 6 planned maintenance windows/year (<=6 hours each) with a required published maintenance calendar 5 business days in advance. Redwood needs an explicit emergency patch carve-out (security patches) with 24 hours notice, and those events will not count against the 6 windows.

4) Response times: 1 hour initial response for Sev1 across all customers; Sev2 4 hours for Enterprise Support or Dedicated; 8 hours for standard. We can include an option to transition Acme to Enterprise Support for an additional fee if they want the 4-hour Sev2 SLA across the board.

Next steps: Lauren will send annotated counter redlines (license/ops carve language) by EOD Wed 6/13. If acceptable, can we aim to have a signed T&Cs + Order Form by 6/30? I'll also drop the annotated PDF in the Drive link above and send a DocuSign envelope once you confirm major points.

Open to a 30-min call tomorrow if it helps finalize open items — please propose times.

Best,
